skill.name: pydantic-models-py
skill.description: Create Pydantic models following the multi-model pattern with Base, Create, Update, Response, and InDB variants. Use when defining API request/response schemas, database models, or data validation in Python applications using Pydantic v2.
skill.summary: Build consistent Pydantic v2 model families for APIs, updates, responses, and database documents.

content.value_statement: API projects need consistent request, response, update, and database schemas. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create Pydantic v2 model families.
actual_capabilities: Defines Base, Create, Update, Response, and InDB model variants.
Shows camelCase aliases with Field aliases and populate_by_name.
Uses optional update fields for PATCH request models.
Adds doc_type fields for database document models.
Prompts users to export models and add matching TypeScript types.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not include executable scripts or generators.
It does not validate existing project schemas automatically.
It focuses on Pydantic v2 patterns, not Pydantic v1 migration.
It does not design database indexes or API routes.

use_cases.title: Start a New API Resource
use_cases.description: Generate a consistent model family for create, update, response, and storage flows.

use_cases.title: Align Backend and Frontend Contracts
use_cases.description: Plan Python schemas with matching TypeScript types for shared API fields.

use_cases.title: Prepare Database Documents
use_cases.description: Add database-facing response variants with doc_type fields for document queries.

prompt_templates.title: Create a New Model Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Create Pydantic v2 models for a [resource] resource. Include Base, Create, Update, Response, and InDB variants using these fields: [fields].

prompt_templates.title: Add Alias Conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the model set to use camelCase API aliases for snake_case fields. Explain which fields need aliases and keep populate_by_name enabled.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Pydantic models for the multi-model pattern. Identify missing variants, optional update fields, response fields, and database document fields.

prompt_templates.title: Design Contract Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this resource schema for a breaking API change. Preserve database compatibility, document affected TypeScript types, and list migration risks.

output_examples.input: Create Project models with name, description, workspace id, owner id, and timestamps.
output_examples.output: A complete model plan with Base, Create, Update, Response, and InDB variants, including alias guidance and database fields.

output_examples.input: Review an Update model where required fields are still mandatory.
output_examples.output: A focused review explaining which update fields should become optional and which response fields should remain required.

output_examples.input: Add a database document variant for a customer resource.
output_examples.output: A storage-focused model variant recommendation that adds a stable document type and keeps API response fields reusable.

best_practices: Provide field names, types, required status, and API direction before generating models.
Confirm naming conventions for camelCase aliases before adding fields.
Review generated models with project validators and tests before merging.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to infer hidden database fields from incomplete requirements.
Do not mix Pydantic v1 and v2 configuration styles in the same model set.
Do not skip TypeScript type updates when API clients depend on matching schemas.

faq.question: Does this skill generate code automatically?
faq.answer: It provides instructions and templates for model creation. The assistant still writes the final model code in your project.

faq.question: Which Pydantic version does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Pydantic v2 patterns, including Field aliases and populate_by_name usage.

faq.question: Can it help with FastAPI schemas?
faq.answer: Yes. The Base, Create, Update, and Response variants map well to common FastAPI request and response schemas.

faq.question: Does it support database models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an InDB variant with a doc_type field for database documents.

faq.question: Will it update TypeScript types?
faq.answer: It reminds the assistant to add matching TypeScript types, but the user must provide project conventions.

faq.question: Does it run commands or access the network?
faq.answer: The skill content does not include scripts, command execution, or network requests.
